title: Type Hinting: Basic & Container Type Annotations

slides.title: Basic & Container Type Hints
slides.prompt: Type hinting improves readability, IDE autocompletion, and static analysis. Python 3.9+ allows using built-in container types directly (`list`, `dict`, `tuple`, `set`) for generics.

slides.title: Function Return Type Hint Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator symbol used to specify the return type of a function.
slides.codeSnippet:
def get_username(user_id: int) ___ str:
    return "User" + str(user_id)

slides.title: Tuple Homogeneous Length Annotation
slides.prompt: How do you specify a variable-length tuple containing integers only in Python 3.9+?

slides.title: List Type Hint Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the generic list type annotation for a list containing float numbers in Python 3.9+.

slides.title: Runtime Enforcement of Type Hints
slides.prompt: Does Python enforce type annotations at runtime by default?
options: No, type hints are ignored at runtime and used primarily by external static analyzers/IDEs
Yes, Python raises a TypeError if an argument does not match its type hint
Yes, but only inside function signatures with explicit return types
No, unless the script is compiled with the -O optimization flag
slides.correctAnswer: No, type hints are ignored at runtime and used primarily by external static analyzers/IDEs
